skill.description: Guides AI video generation with the inference.sh CLI, including text-to-video, image-to-video, avatar, lipsync, foley, upscaling, and video merging workflows.
skill.summary: Generate AI video workflows through inference.sh CLI examples and model guidance.
skill.author: tul-sh

security_audit.summary: Most backtick and hardcoded URL detections are false positives from Markdown formatting, model identifiers, placeholder media URLs, and documentation links. Several command examples are confirmed because they direct users or agents to run infsh or skill-install commands that contact external services. No prompt injection text or hidden exfiltration logic was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.suggestion: State that infsh commands require explicit user approval and may send prompts, images, audio, or video to external services.
Replace broad npx skills add examples with reviewed documentation links or immutable references for each recommended skill.
Use a marketplace-hosted image asset or clearly document that the remote image loads from cloud.inference.sh.
Label example image, audio, and video URLs as placeholders and remind users not to submit private media without review.

content.value_statement: Teams need repeatable prompts for video models without memorizing each CLI app. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through inference.sh video workflows.
actual_capabilities: Lists text-to-video models such as Veo, Grok, and Seedance with app IDs.
Provides infsh commands for text-to-video prompts and model selection.
Shows image-to-video, avatar, lipsync, foley, upscaling, and merging examples.
Points users to inference.sh documentation for running apps and streaming results.
Suggests related skills for narration, image generation, and posting workflows.
limitations: Requires an installed and authenticated inference.sh CLI.
Does not include a local video renderer or model weights.
Video quality, cost, duration, and policies depend on selected third-party apps.
Examples use placeholder URLs that users must replace with accessible media.

use_cases.title: Draft Social Video Concepts
use_cases.description: Generate short video ideas and commands for platform-ready clips using text-to-video models.

use_cases.title: Animate Product Visuals
use_cases.description: Turn approved product images into motion concepts with image-to-video workflows.

use_cases.title: Prepare Avatar Narration
use_cases.description: Use avatar and lipsync examples to plan talking-head videos from portrait and audio assets.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner Text-to-Video
prompt_templates.scenario: Create a first video prompt with a fast model.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create a short text-to-video prompt for a calm product reveal. Recommend a suitable inference.sh model and explain the command inputs.

prompt_templates.title: Image Animation Setup
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare an image-to-video job from a source image.
prompt_templates.prompt: I have a product image URL and want subtle camera motion. Choose an image-to-video model and outline the inputs I need before running infsh.

prompt_templates.title: Avatar Video Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Plan a talking-head or lipsync clip.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an avatar video workflow using a portrait and narration audio. Compare OmniHuman, Fabric, and PixVerse for this case.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced Content Pipeline
prompt_templates.scenario: Combine generation, sound, upscaling, and merging.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a multi-step inference.sh plan for a campaign video with generated clips, foley sound, upscaling, and final merging. Include checkpoints for review.

output_examples.input: A user asks for a five-second beach sunset video with wave motion.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends a text-to-video model, refines the visual prompt, and identifies the duration field to set before running the CLI.

output_examples.input: A designer has a portrait image and narration audio for a training module.
output_examples.output: The skill compares avatar and lipsync options, lists required media inputs, and flags privacy review before submission.

output_examples.input: A marketing team wants to upscale and merge two generated clips.
output_examples.output: The skill suggests the upscaler and media merger apps, then describes a review order for quality checks and final assembly.

best_practices: Confirm media rights and privacy approval before submitting images, audio, or video URLs.
Start with fast preview models before spending time or credits on higher quality models.
Save prompts, model names, and output settings so successful results can be repeated.
anti_patterns: Do not submit private client media to external models without explicit approval.
Do not assume placeholder URLs work without replacing them with accessible assets.
Do not install related skills unless their source and permissions have been reviewed.

faq.question: Does this skill generate video locally?
faq.answer: No. It guides inference.sh CLI commands that call hosted video generation apps.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What do I need before using it?
faq.answer: You need the inference.sh CLI installed, authenticated, and available as infsh.

faq.question: Can it animate existing images?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes image-to-video examples for Wan and Seedance models.

faq.question: Can it make talking-head videos?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents avatar and lipsync options such as OmniHuman, Fabric, and PixVerse.

faq.question: Are there privacy considerations?
faq.answer: Yes. Prompts and media URLs may be sent to external services when commands run.
